newsitem.title: USA: Senate panel may take up muni arbitrage - senator.
newsitem.headline: Senate panel may take up muni arbitrage - senator.

text.p: U.S. Sen. Bob Graham said Thursday he got positive feedback from Senate Finance Committee aides to his request that key arbitrage rebate simplification proposals appear in draft tax legislation.

"They were generally positive," Graham told reporters after a speech at a Council for Infrastructure Financing Authorities conference. "His staff thought these were reasonable ideas," said Graham, a Florida Democrat who sits on the Senate Finance Committee.
Graham said finance panel staff members do think that his proposals would "have a positive impact" in stimulating much needed school construction and repairs.
Staff also thinks the proposals are "within the dollar amounts" that the panel could allocate to education-related matters, Graham said.

The senator said six or seven of the nine Democrats on the finance panel, which is chaired by Delaware Republican William Roth, have already signed on to his proposal. He added that several Republicans on the panel have "indicated an interest."
Graham said the Republicans want to see estimates of the provisions' costs before signing on. A joint House-Senate commitee on taxation is expected to provide those estimates shortly.
Graham is hoping that the broad tax package being drafted by Roth following Capitol Hill's balanced budget pact will include his four provisions.

Two of Graham's provisions are arbitrage rebate proposals avidly sought by state and local governments. They are excluded from a tax package being considered this week by the House Ways and Means Committee.
They would raise the small issuer rebate exception from $5 million to $25 million and provide a rebate safe harbor for long term fixed-rate debt.
Graham's package also would create a new category of tax exempt activity bonds for educational activities and make the category exempt from the volume cap.
It would permit the use of accelerated depreciation for facilities that are financed with the new exempt activity educational bonds.
And it would the raise from $10 million to $25 million the amount of bonds a state or local government can issue annually for purchase by banks.
Graham presented the package as a school construction initiative. But he made clear that funds could be used for other tax exempt financings.
